samples.summary: New frontend `seg()` id-pinning guard is bypassed by every other browser API module that interpolates the same route-param ids
samples.evidence: The change introduces `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` and applies `seg()` only inside `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts`. The same document/workspace/folder ids (which reach these modules from the URL bar and pasted links, exactly the source the new doc comment cites) are still interpolated raw into session-carrying `fetchWithAuth` calls elsewhere: `packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:60` and `:78` (`/documents/${documentId}/share-links`), `:89` (`/share-links/${id}`); `packages/frontend/src/api/files.ts:22` (`/documents/${documentId}/file`); `packages/frontend/src/api/analytics.ts:127` (`/documents/${documentId}/analytics`); `packages/frontend/src/api/folders.ts:42,64,82`; `packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:48,75,88,184,196,212` (incl. `/${workspaceId}/api-keys/${keyId}`); `packages/frontend/src/api/datasources.ts:45,65,78,90,104`. A `..`-bearing id reaching any of these walks the request off the intended endpoint with the user's session attached — the precise condition the new guard exists to stop. Fix belongs at these call sites (add `seg()`), not in the new module.

samples.summary: New `assertFetchableImageUrl` host guard can break existing `docs export` / `slides export` runs against self-hosted or split-origin deployments
samples.evidence: `createImageFetcher` is consumed by `packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261` and `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209`, both passing only `getConfig(opts).server` as the exemption origin. Any image `src` that is an absolute URL on an origin other than the configured `--server` and resolves to a private/loopback address is now a hard failure of the whole export: self-hosted installs where blobs/images are served by a separate internal host or port (e.g. MinIO/S3 at `http://10.0.0.5:9000`, a reverse proxy on a second port), and the common `--server http://localhost:3000` vs stored `http://127.0.0.1:3000/...` spelling mismatch (different origins, so `sameOriginAsServer` fails and `isPrivateHost` refuses). Previously these fetched fine. Backend-generated URLs are relative (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:74`) so the default path is safe, but documents imported/edited with absolute srcs are not.

samples.summary: Frontend `seg()` throws a bare `Error`, bypassing the `assertOk`/toast error contract every other failure in these modules uses
samples.evidence: `fetchDocument`/`renameDocument`/`moveDocument`/`copyDocument`/`deleteDocument` previously only ever rejected with the `assertOk`-produced HttpError (with its toast/message handling used by callers such as `packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx` and the mutations in `packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx`). For a `.`/`..` id they now reject before any fetch with `new Error('Invalid path segment: ".."')`, which those consumers' error handling was not written for (no toast, generic message). Frontend has no `tsc`/typed-error lane to surface this.

finding.summary: New frontend `seg()` id-pinning guard is bypassed by every other browser API module that interpolates the same route-param ids
finding.evidence: The change introduces `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` and applies `seg()` only inside `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts`. The same document/workspace/folder ids (which reach these modules from the URL bar and pasted links, exactly the source the new doc comment cites) are still interpolated raw into session-carrying `fetchWithAuth` calls elsewhere: `packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:60` and `:78` (`/documents/${documentId}/share-links`), `:89` (`/share-links/${id}`); `packages/frontend/src/api/files.ts:22` (`/documents/${documentId}/file`); `packages/frontend/src/api/analytics.ts:127` (`/documents/${documentId}/analytics`); `packages/frontend/src/api/folders.ts:42,64,82`; `packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:48,75,88,184,196,212` (incl. `/${workspaceId}/api-keys/${keyId}`); `packages/frontend/src/api/datasources.ts:45,65,78,90,104`. A `..`-bearing id reaching any of these walks the request off the intended endpoint with the user's session attached — the precise condition the new guard exists to stop. verdict.reason: The finding is accurate in every checkable respect. `seg()` is defined at packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts:18-23 and a repo-wide grep for `seg(` shows it is applied ONLY in documents.ts (lines 47,65,88,110,155) and url.ts itself. All cited bypassing sites interpolate ids raw, verbatim as quoted: share-links.ts:60,78,89; analytics.ts:127; folders.ts:42,64,82 (also 10,24); files.ts:22; workspaces.ts:48,75,88,184,196,212 (incl. `/${workspaceId}/api-keys/${keyId}`); datasources.ts:45,65,78,90,104 — plus additional unlisted sites (miro.ts:93, workspaces.ts:102,115,130,143,227,272,291,304,316). Every one routes through `fetchWithAuth`, which sets `credentials: "include"` unconditionally at auth.ts:141-144, so the session is attached exactly as the guard's own doc comment (url.ts:7-11) warns. Reachability from the URL bar is concrete: document-analytics.tsx:45 useParams `id` feeds analytics.ts:127; workspace-settings.tsx:51 and workspace-datasources.tsx:13 useParams `workspaceId` feed the raw workspaces.ts/datasources.ts calls; share-dialog.tsx:84,117,145 feeds share-links.ts. I found no upstream sanitiser pinning these route-param ids, so `already-guarded` does not apply. This is squarely the blast-radius lane: a new guard added in one module with other entry points reaching the same operation without it — a finding that cannot be stated from the diff alone. `major` is a fair (if conservative) severity for a reachable guard bypass.

finding.summary: New `assertFetchableImageUrl` host guard can break existing `docs export` / `slides export` runs against self-hosted or split-origin deployments
finding.evidence: `createImageFetcher` is consumed by `packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261` and `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209`, both passing only `getConfig(opts).server` as the exemption origin. Any image `src` that is an absolute URL on an origin other than the configured `--server` and resolves to a private/loopback address is now a hard failure of the whole export: self-hosted installs where blobs/images are served by a separate internal host or port (e.g. MinIO/S3 at `http://10.0.0.5:9000`, a reverse proxy on a second port), and the common `--server http://localhost:3000` vs stored `http://127.0.0.1:3000/...` spelling mismatch (different origins, so `sameOriginAsServer` fails and `isPrivateHost` refuses). Previously these fetched fine. Backend-generated URLs are relative (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:74`) so the default path is safe, but documents imported/edited with absolute srcs are not.

verdict.reason: The guard is present as described: assertFetchableImageUrl (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:111-133) rejects any http(s) image URL that is not exactly same-origin with serverBase when the host is loopback/private (isPrivateHost, lines 45-66), and createImageFetcher applies it to every image (line 151). Both consumers pass only the configured server as the sole exemption origin (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261-263, packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209), with no allowlist and no per-image soft-fail, so the throw aborts the entire export. The reviewer's premise is corroborated more strongly than claimed: although the backend emits relative URLs (packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:74, packages/backend/src/image/image.service.ts:128), the frontend deliberately rewrites them to ABSOLUTE URLs before persisting into the document (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:12-18,39 and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:46,86-90), prefixing VITE_BACKEND_API_URL, documented in-code as 'http://localhost:3000' in dev and a separate origin in every shipped environment; docs image insertion goes through that uploader (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:11-14). Therefore stored srcs are routinely absolute loopback/private-host URLs, and any spelling/port/host divergence from --server (127.0.0.1 vs localhost, internal vs external API host) now hard-fails docs/slides export that previously worked. This is a behaviour change to an exported symbol breaking existing consumer flows — in the blast-radius lane, reachable, and no guard elsewhere normalises the origin.
